Points are VIC X and raster line: a bitmap pixel (xb, yb) is vic_x xb + 24, line yb + 51; band line L is bitmap row 36 + L. The three rows are the twister recipe's measured table (first and last lit pixel); the overlap pixels are inside the vector-balls recipe's ball 0 over ball 1 rectangle (PAL columns 232 to 240, rows 131 to 143), which read 96 white and 18 grey here as on the recipe's page. NTSC note: the NTSC half-copy fix means that at frame 300 the top 60 band lines (0..59) carry phase 42 on NTSC (drawn at t=298, even frame) while the bottom 68 lines (60..127) carry phase 43 (drawn at t=299, odd frame). Checks for specific lit-pixel positions on band lines 0 and 40 are PAL-only because those lines are in the top half and their phase-specific positions differ by one step between PAL (phase 43) and NTSC (phase 42). Band line 100 is in the bottom half and passes on both models. The same-area check is PAL-only because the top and bottom halves carry consecutive phases on NTSC, so the band area differs from PAL.
